title: PaperTrail Fintech — pilot soundboard and outbound drafts
content:
Context: quick internal scratch for PaperTrail Fintech — a mid‑market payments/ledger startup (YC S18 style) exploring embedded risk scoring + reconciliation automation. Goal: get a 6‑8 week pilot for inference-backed chat and batch reconciliation suggestions (hosted or dedicated). This file = messy soundboard: account facts, outreach language variations, call bullets, and common objections + counters. Use as starting point for AE outreach.

Account snapshot (what I could dig up):
- HQ: Austin, TX; Series B (2023), ~220 employees; vertical: payments + reconciliation for platform merchants.
- Recent news: launched "SmartSettlements" (Nov 2025) — automated settlement matching; hiring in data infra and risk.
- Likely PM/eng champions: "Aria Patel" (Head of Data), "Ben Kwan" (Dir. Engineering, Payments). CFO-ish: "Laura Weiss" (VP Finance) who cares about cost/unit and audit trail.
- Tech signals: uses AWS, Kafka, Postgres; calls out "latency constraints for merchant-facing dashboards" in job posts; references to open models / LLM integration in engineering blog (opt-in to third‑party inference).
- Pain to target: reconciliation suggestions are noisy (rule-based), support load spikes at daily batch close, and merchants complain about opaque risk flags.

Product fit hypothesis (how Redwood could help):
- Replace / augment rule-based reconciler with a scoring + suggestion LLM for ambiguous matches (reduce manual review).
- Use streaming chat for merchant-facing troubleshooting assistant (latency SLOs matter).
- For pilot: 1) batch inference for daily reconciliation suggestions (non‑PII sample), 2) realtime chat stub for 10 merchants.
- Deployment mode: start hosted API for speed, then Dedicated if audit/throughput/cost demands appear.

Key asks for pilot:
- 6–8 week sandbox, 2 engineers + 1 product PM committed; dataset access: 30 days of de‑identified reconciliation logs; SLO target: <= 350ms median for merchant chat; acceptance metric: 25% reduction in manual review volume or 15% faster settlement resolution.

Outbound drafts (pick variant depending on tone):
1) Short cold email (concise, founder tone)
Subject: quick idea to cut reconciliation review by 25%
Hi Aria — saw SmartSettlements launch, congrats. We help fintech teams replace brittle reconciliation rules with inference-backed suggestions that reduce manual reviews and speed settlements. Can I share a 2‑page pilot plan tailored to SmartSettlements? 15 min next week?
—Maya (Redwood Inference)

2) Longer email (technical + proof points)
Subject: 2‑week pilot idea — inference for ambiguous reconciliation cases
Aria — quick note: we worked with a payments platform to cut manual reconciliation by 32% using a small LLM model + prefix caching and targeted batching (hosted→dedicated). We can run a scoped pilot on a de‑identified slice of your daily batch and show error/suggestion precision vs. current rules. No heavy infra changes; most teams start on hosted API then move Dedicated for throughput. If useful I can send a one‑pager + proposed dataset schema.

3) LinkedIn/voicemail script (casual)
Hey Aria — Maya from Redwood Inference. We help teams reduce reconciliation toil with inference suggestions that integrate into existing QA flows. Would love 10 minutes to share a pilot plan — will email a note as well.

Call prep bullets (for first intro):
- 30s intro: Redwood intro + quick customer stat (cut manual review 30% typical).
- 60s pitch: pilot scope, target metric, required commitment (dataset + 2 engineers).
- Questions: current review volume (avg/day), current mean time to settle, what data they can share (PII concerns), existing infra limits (QPS, redis/KV cache), internal champions and procurement timeline.
- Risk/cost de‑risk: offer hosted sandbox + limited token cap; outline path to Dedicated if throughput grows.

Common objections + counters (raw):
- Objection: "We can't share data / security"
  Counter: sandbox with de‑identified slice; optional Private deployment (VPC) or dedicated instance; sign standard DPA, SOC2 checklist; we can run inference on customer-managed compute for on‑prem cases.
- Objection: "Latencies will kill merchant UX"
  Counter: explain Redwood optimizations: prefix/KV caching, batching windows tuned for reconciliation vs chat, and streaming for the chat piece. Start with non‑real‑time batch to build trust; show benchmarks for similar customers.
- Objection: "Fees look high vs internal infra"
  Counter: total cost of manual review + slow settlements often larger; present a quick ROI table: time saved * avg FTE cost vs monthly inference spend; highlight Dedicated reserved capacity option for predictable unit cost.
- Objection: "Model hallucinations / compliance risk"
  Counter: guardrails: deterministic templates for suggestions, eval sets for precision/regression alerts in Redwood Optimize; human-in-loop acceptance for first N weeks.

Data / legal checklist to ask for (early):
- Can we get a de‑identified 30‑day sample? fields: transaction_id, merchant_id (hashed), amount, timestamp, reconciliation_status, supporting_text (redact PII), existing_rule_score, human_decision (if available).
- SLA/legal: DPA + SOC2 or Private VPC? Who owns signing?

Quick ROI sketch (for email):
- Baseline: 400 ambiguous matches/day, avg review = 8min -> 53 FTE hours/wk.
- Goal: 25% reducer -> save ~13 FTE hours/wk. At $80/hr fully loaded -> $54k/mo. Price pilot/monthly inference = $6k -> net positive. (tailor numbers in one‑pager).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Diego: can you pull one anonymized 7‑day sample schema from the platform example we used in TP-1423? (JIRA-ENG-9876)
- Ask legal for a lightweight DPA template for pilot — Ava to ping legal #contracts.
- Draft one‑pager with dataset schema and bench numbers — Samir to take baseline ROI table.
- Decide initial outreach channel: Aria (LinkedIn + email) or Ben (direct to eng). Personal gut: start with Aria.

Notes to self (casual):
- Keep pilot small & measurable. Avoid "LLM will replace rules" messaging — focus on "assist & prioritise".
- If they care deeply about audit trails, push Private/Dedicated early.
- Use customer story from payments platform (TP-1423) but avoid overclaiming numbers — present ranges and percent reductions.

End of notes.

---
